chunks: Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ibn Muskān from 'Ubayd Allah al-Halabi said:

I asked Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the prayer of the eclipse: is it compensated if it is missed? He said, 'There is no compensation for it.' And we had previously held that it is compensated, so the meaning of this report is that if the disk [of the sun] is not entirely consumed, but if it is entirely consumed, then compensation is necessary according to what we have previously stated, and to add clarification to it is what he narrated:
ai.seo_question: Is the eclipse prayer required to be made up if missed?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies a nuance in the eclipse prayer ruling, stating that missed prayers are not compensated for when the eclipse is partial, resolving earlier assumptions that all eclipses required *qada*. This distinction highlights the Shia scholarly approach to reconciling apparent contradictions in hadith by differentiating between total and partial celestial phenomena. The ruling underscores the principle that the obligation to make up the prayer is contingent upon the completeness of the obscuration, reflecting a precise legal methodology.
